text:
maria: hi everyone, day 2 and I'm stuck — i downloaded the kubeconfig zip from the onboarding portal and appended it to my existing ~/.kube/config. now `kubectl config get-contexts` shows two contexts both named `redwood-dev` and when i `kubectl use-context redwood-dev` it switches to the wrong one (i think prod?). any quick way to tell which context is which before i run anything risky?

ben: welcome! short answer: check the cluster field in the context and the user. `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` then `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[*].name} {.contexts[*].context.cluster} {.contexts[*].context.user}'` helps. but easier: use `KUBECONFIG` with separate files instead of merging.

maria: oh nice — i don't know how to split the file out. i only have one combined file now.

devex-bot: onboarding doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/onboarding/k8s#safe-kubeconfig
Tip: create `~/.kube/contexts/` and put each cluster file there, then `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml:~/.kube/contexts/common.yaml` to avoid name collisions. Also consider `kubectx` for friendly names.

maria: trying `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="redwood-dev")].context.cluster}'` returned `arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:123456:cluster/redwood-prod` so yeah that's definitely not dev :grimacing:

ops-engineer: yikes. if you accidentally hit prod please stop and ping #eng-oncall. we have protections but still want to audit. i'll help you clean this up — can you paste the output of `kubectl config view --flatten --raw` (masked tokens ok) into a Gist and share?

maria: posted gist: https://gists.example/abcd (i redacted certs)

ops-engineer: thanks. i see duplicate context names because the portal file used `redwood-dev` and your old config also used the same. i'll create a safe copy for you: `~/.kube/contexts/redwood-dev-portal.yaml` and rewrite the context name to `redwood-dev-portal` with `kubectl config rename-context redwood-dev redwood-dev-portal --kubeconfig=~/.kube/contexts/redwood-dev-portal.yaml`.

maria: do i need to run that? i'd rather not touch the original file.

ben: ops-engineer can modify the copied file remotely or give instructions. the safe approach: move the combined file to a backup: `mv ~/.kube/config ~/.kube/config.bak` then split the files into `dev.yaml` and `prod.yaml` by copying the portal content into `~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml`. don't paste creds in chat.

security-bot: FYI: if you accessed prod accidentally, our audit will record API calls under your identity. If you believe any prod write happened, open an incident.

maria: confirmed i didn't run any writes. once ops-engineer gave the steps i moved the portal kubeconfig to `~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml` and set `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml:~/.kube/config.bak`. `kubectl config get-contexts` now shows distinct names. thanks!

ops-engineer: one more: we intentionally prefix portal contexts with `portal-<team>` to avoid collisions, but older configs sometimes clash. if you want i can request a short-lived rolebinding for `maria@redwood` in `team-maria` namespace so you can test permissions without touching cluster-wide resources — reply with portal ticket id to expedite.

maria: ticket ONB-501 is open. would love the temp rolebinding.

ops-engineer: done: created RoleBinding `rb-onboard-maria` for user `maria@redwood` in namespace `team-maria`, role `view`, expires 48h. check `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-maria`.

maria: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-maria` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-maria` -> lists pods. all good :relieved:

ben: pro tip: add `alias kdev='KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml kubectl --context=redwood-dev-portal'` to your shellrc to avoid accidental context switches.

maria: adding that now. thanks for the help everyone! closing this thread.
